Subject: Post-demo recap: migrating from legacy GPU cluster — hosting fit & PoC next steps

Samantha / Michael — thanks again for the demo time earlier. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to track decisions.

Summary of needs you shared
- Current: on-prem legacy GPU cluster running a mix of Triton + custom scheduler, serving ~150 qps at peak for shorter sequences.
- Pain points: manual scaling, tail latency spikes during bursts, expensive headroom, and strict PHI/data residency rules for a subset of traffic.
- Goals: move off the legacy cluster over the next 3–4 months, preserve latency SLAs (~<120ms 95th for short chat flows), and meet SOC2/KMS controls for regulated datasets.

Hosting options we discussed
1) Hosted API (Redwood hosted): fastest time-to-value; good for dev/low-risk pilot but you noted PHI restrictions block production for some flows.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool): keeps predictable throughput, isolation of compute, and lower unit costs — suitable if you want Redwood-managed infrastructure but isolated to Atlas.
3) Private VPC / On‑prem package: customer-managed network and KMS/HSM integrations — best fit for regulated production traffic where data cannot traverse third-party networks.

Migration modes we proposed
- Lift & shift with model compatibility layer (fastest): push identical model weights to Redwood Dedicated; minimal model surgery but requires validation of KV-cache behavior.
- Replatform + compile pass (recommended where cost matters): convert to a Redwood-optimized runtime, apply quantization profiles, recompile kernels for target cards — better cost/latency but needs validation.
- Hybrid split routing: keep sensitive traffic on Private, non-PHI traffic to Hosted/Dedicated for cost savings.

Proposed PoC scope (3 weeks) — deliverables
- Week 0: access & onboarding (service accounts, network allowlist, small sample dataset)
- Week 1: reproduce baseline traffic with a traffic replay of 10k requests, capture latency/cost baselines on Dedicated config
- Week 2: apply quantization profile + prefix caching; measure 95th latency and token cost delta
- Week 3: deployment test including canary, rollback, and short run of sensitive workload on a Private VPC proof of connectivity

Immediate asks for Atlas from our side
- Provide a short sample of representative request traces (anonymized), max sequence length, and typical concurrency distribution.
- Confirm whether PHI applies to a single product line or across all endpoints.

Next steps
- I will share a one-page SOW + security summary for the PoC (attached).
- Ben / Karthik from my team are looped for the technical kickoff; Ben will lead the Dedicated config and Karthik will scope Private/VPC rough effort.

If that all looks right, can we lock the PoC start window for the week of May 18?

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

A few clarifications from our side:
- PHI scope: currently three endpoints ingest PHI (claims parsing, patient note summarization, and auth flows). Those must remain in an environment with our KMS and egress controls — sounds like Private VPC is the only route for those.
- Traffic patterns: peak bursts happen in business hours with sudden bursts (150 qps -> 400 qps sustained for 10–20 minutes). We can provide anonymized traces by tomorrow.
- Timeline: engineering prefers a non-disruptive migration and wants to see Dedicated run costs before committing to Private (procurement will need cost numbers).

We are ok to run the PoC week of May 18 provided Redwood can support a Private connectivity test (VPN or VPC peering) and a Dedicated test bed. Please include a short estimate for Dedicated hourly spend so procurement can review.

—Samantha

Camila / team / Samantha — quick reply with answers and next steps so the PoC SOW can be finalized.

Dedicated estimate (ballpark)
- Baseline pool: 4 x A10g-equivalent nodes reserved for the PoC, burst to 8 for traffic replay windows.
- Estimated hourly infra: $45/hr baseline pool, $90/hr peak (burst engaged). For a week-long test with the defined replay profile we estimate ~$8k–$12k infra spend depending on actual burst. Exact token-level cost depends on sequence length and the quantization profile; we'll refine once we have traces.

Private VPC connectivity & KMS
- Connectivity options: VPC peering preferred (lowest latency) — requires route table updates and a shared VPC CIDR plan. VPN is supported for quick tests but adds ~40–80ms RTT overhead.
- KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) for encrypting model artifacts and disk volumes. HSM integrations need separate legal/security review for key escrow requirements; for a PoC we recommend customer-managed KMS with a service-account role.
- Rough standup time: VPC peering test endpoint ~2–3 business days once we have network info and ACLs; VPN can be live same-day with your network team.

Blocked items we need from Atlas
- Anonymized trace file + concurrency profile (Samantha said available tomorrow)
- CIDR ranges for peering or VPN config
- Confirmation on which endpoints must stay in Private for PHI so we can scope split routing in the PoC

I'll attach a simple cost worksheet and a one-page connectivity checklist to the SOW Camila is assembling. Camila — I'll send the updated SOW + estimated numbers by EOD so procurement can review.

Ben Carter
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
